q: How does the AMR plasmid and mobilome diversity of MDR Aeromonas veronii differ between farmed (aquaculture) and wild Bangladeshi stinging catfish (Heteropneustes fossilis), and how strongly is that diversity linked to on-farm antibiotic selection pressure?
basis: Rahman 2023 characterised a single Alim_AV_1000 isolate from a farmed source, deposited under BioProject PRJNA810265 / GCF_026738955.1. Our replication independently confirmed a chromosomal beta-lactam resistome (OXA-12 / blaOXA-12 / ampS at 97.59% identity, cphA4 subclass-B2 metallo-beta-lactamase at 96.19%, plus the MDR-efflux regulator rsmA) via five-way abricate concordance (CARD, NCBI-AMR, ResFinder, ARGannot, MEGARes) but the paper's specific tetracycline-family gene claim did not pass default thresholds, and the paper studied only one isolate.
next_steps: Sample paired farm-vs-wild Shing catfish (Heteropneustes fossilis) at matched sites in Mymensingh/Bogura/Rajshahi, isolate multiple A. veronii per fish, do hybrid short+long-read sequencing to close plasmids, run MOB-suite / plasmidSPAdes / PlasmidFinder to catalogue the mobilome, and correlate plasmid presence/AMR gene load with on-farm antibiotic use logs (oxytetracycline, sulfonamide, quinolone) collected via a structured farm questionnaire.

q: How often does MDR A. veronii from farmed stinging catfish (Shing fish) actually cross into human wound infections in Bangladeshi fish-handling communities, and are cross-host isolates genomically distinct from fish-only isolates?
basis: Rahman 2023 emphasises the zoonotic potential of MDR A. veronii from Shing catfish (a fish handled bare-handed by farmers and market sellers, whose dorsal spines are known to cause puncture wounds) but the paper itself only sequences a single fish-source isolate. Our replication confirmed the strain is A. veronii (ANI 96.34%-96.47% to sister strains TH0426 and B565), MDR at the genotype level (OXA-12 + cphA4), and encodes a full virulence toolkit (T2SS 9 genes / T3SS 37 genes / T6SS 16 genes / hemolysin-adjacent flagellar + adhesin systems), any of which would be relevant to wound infection --- but no human isolates were characterised.
next_steps: Prospective enrollment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital + district hospitals in Mymensingh/Sylhet: culture wound swabs from fisher/farmer/market-worker patients presenting with post-handling infections, sequence any A. veronii isolates, and compare (core-genome MLST + ANI + AMR gene set + plasmid content) against contemporaneous fish-source A. veronii isolates from the same catchment; use SNP distance and shared-plasmid analysis to bound plausible fish-to-human transmission events.

q: Does the hemolysin / aerolysin / T3SS virulence-gene repertoire vary across A. veronii lineages in a way that predicts a fish-pathogenicity gradient (asymptomatic carriage vs. motile aeromonad septicaemia in Shing fish)?
basis: Our replication of Rahman 2023 detected a full T3SS (37 asc/acr genes), a full T6SS (16 vipA/atsG-S/vasH-K/hcp/clpB genes), 40 polar and 17 lateral flagellar genes, and MSHA/Tap/type-I pili --- but Alim_AV_1000 is only one lineage and Rahman 2023 did not test experimental fish pathogenicity. The clinical relevance of exactly which subset (aerolysin variants, T3SS effector complement, hemolysin allele) drives severe disease in stinging catfish is unresolved.
next_steps: Assemble a diverse A. veronii panel (10-20 isolates spanning fish-disease-severe, fish-asymptomatic-carrier, environment, and human sources), do pangenome analysis (roary/panaroo) focused on aerolysin/hemolysin/T3SS effector gene family, then run controlled challenge in juvenile Heteropneustes fossilis at BLSRI or BAU Mymensingh with matched inoculum, scoring mortality and organ colonisation; fit a lineage->pathogenicity regression on the aerolysin/T3SS-effector genotype.

q: How readily does the AMR gene reservoir of MDR A. veronii in Bangladeshi stinging-catfish aquaculture undergo horizontal gene transfer into native co-inhabitant pathogens (Vibrio spp., Edwardsiella tarda / ictaluri, Aeromonas hydrophila) in the same pond?
basis: Rahman 2023 documents an MDR A. veronii genome with a chromosomal beta-lactam resistome, and our replication confirmed OXA-12 + cphA4 + rsmA. But cphA is a subclass-B2 metallo-beta-lactamase and rsmA regulates efflux, and neither is on a mobile element we characterised. The paper does not measure whether these genes (or accompanying plasmid-borne AMR loci that were not detected in our default-threshold sweep) mobilise into other pond pathogens.
next_steps: Water/sediment/co-cultured-fish sampling from Shing polyculture ponds in Mymensingh and Jessore, isolate A. veronii + V. cholerae/parahaemolyticus + E. tarda / E. ictaluri from the same pond, sequence, and (i) map shared AMR/plasmid backbones across genera; (ii) do in vitro filter-mating conjugation between plasmid-bearing A. veronii and marked recipient Vibrio/Edwardsiella; (iii) measure transfer frequency with and without sub-inhibitory oxytetracycline; report the reservoir->recipient transfer rate.

q: Under alternative aquaculture antibiotic-use regimes (unrestricted vs. regulated tetracycline / sulfonamide / no-antibiotic + probiotic), how does the A. veronii AMR gene reservoir change over 12-24 months on Bangladeshi Shing catfish farms?
basis: Rahman 2023 identifies MDR A. veronii on a working farm; our replication confirmed the genome-encoded beta-lactam resistome but did not replicate the paper's specific tetracycline-family gene call at default abricate thresholds. This leaves the dynamics of the AMR reservoir under different treatment regimes untested. Bangladesh currently has limited enforcement of aquaculture antibiotic guidelines and no longitudinal AMR surveillance for Aeromonas.
next_steps: Cluster-randomised 24-month intervention across 20-30 farms in three arms (arm A: current unrestricted use; arm B: DoF-guideline-restricted oxytetracycline only; arm C: no antibiotic + Bacillus/lactic-acid probiotic protocol), quarterly fish + water + sediment sampling with A. veronii isolation and short-read sequencing, per-arm mixed-effects modelling of change in AMR gene prevalence (tet, sul, bla, qnr) over time, and a costed policy brief for the Bangladesh Department of Fisheries.
